triage.verifier_justification: The only encoded value the commit touches is the single version's `effective_to`, moved from 2025-06-30 to 2023-08-31, and the companion cases move from period 2025-06 to 2023-05 to stay inside the narrowed window — so encoded meaning (which months resolve to the pre-FRA "under 18 or 50 or over" criterion) really changed, which rules out mechanical/test_only, and no other kind fits a pure version-window change (it is not a comparison-strictness flip, a missing clause, or an entity/scope change). The commit message states the fidelity failure directly: the prior bound "preserved a legally obsolete result across the FRA phase-in," i.e. every month from September 2023 through June 2025 asserted criteria P.L. 118-5 §311(a)(1) had already struck from the federal text this manual provision mirrors. My refutation attempts do not land: the pinned corpus confirms current 7 U.S.C. 2015(o)(3) reads "under 18, or over 65, years of age;" with no 50-year exception, so a version alive past the supersession asserts law that no longer existed, and "no consumers / out of FY2026 scope" bears on severity, not on whether the encoded window disagreed with the source. The residual doubt — enough to keep confidence below 0.9 — is that the FRA application-date evidence lives in USLM amendment notes that are not registered provision rows (unresolvable through the pinned resolver), and the module's primary cited source, MPP 63-410.321, still reads "Under 18 or 50 years of age or over;" at the pinned corpus, so the exact choice of 2023-08-31 over 2025-06-30 rests on federal supersession reasoning rather than on a change in the cited state text.
